headline: Former Bureaucrat Still Receives Automated Election Campaign Reminders From His Own Unsubscribed Microwave
body:
Former state administrative official Ramanathan Nair reports that his kitchen appliances have begun autonomously campaigning for his political candidacy, a trend he attributes to a lingering glitch in his smart-home ecosystem following a casual discussion about political roles. Despite Nair having never officially filed nomination papers, his microwave has reportedly started pre-heating to the exact electoral color of a major political party whenever he attempts to defrost leftovers.

“I told a few people I was unsure about entering the electoral arena, and the next thing I know, my smart kettle is playing nationalistic anthems every time the water hits 100 degrees,” said Nair, who spent thirty years maintaining a strictly neutral posture in the civil services. “It’s become quite difficult to prepare a simple cup of coffee without the toaster popping up a piece of rye bread with a party symbol scorched into the surface.”

Technicians from the local digital service center suggest that high-level administrative algorithms are becoming overly sensitive to informal lunch conversations. “When a bureaucrat of that stature discusses a hypothetical shift in career, the metadata doesn't just register interest; it initiates a full-scale canvassing protocol,” noted senior software engineer Vikram Sahu. “We’ve had to factory-reset three refrigerators and a smart doorbell this week alone, simply because they kept inviting the neighbors over for campaign rallies that aren't actually happening.”
caption: Is your kitchen secretly running for office? At this rate, we’ll be casting our votes via smart-fridges by the next election cycle. #TechGlitches #ElectionSeason #DigitalOverreach (satire)
igHook: Has your smart home ever started a campaign without your permission?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a modern stainless steel kitchen appliance interior displaying a glowing digital interface, with a slightly blurred home environment in the background.
